title: Chelsea Player Ratings vs. Tottenham: Palmer Sent Off in Disastrous Derby
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray2:47 PM EDTCole Palmer cost his team. / Ryan Pierse/Getty ImagesChelsea suffered only their second home league defeat to Tottenham Hotspur in the last 36 years on Saturday after being comfortably beaten 2–0 by their London rivals.

The Blues were searching for their third successive victory since the international break, but the surprise absence of João Pedro completely disrupted their flow. Despite the goalless scoreline in the first half,  Spurs, rather surprisingly, were the superior side at a rain-soaked Stamford Bridge, with Xabi Alonso’s side lacking their usual attacking spark.

It was the same story after the restart for Chelsea as they huffed and puffed with no reward, relying on Tottenham’s profligacy and a possible moment of inspiration. Things would soon get much, much worse, however.

A comical own goal from Mike Penders on his first Premier League start gifted Tottenham a deserved lead, before Cole Palmer was sent off for two quick-fire yellow cards. The first came when he could have been shown a straight red for petulantly barging Mateus Fernandes off the ball, while the second was awarded for an idiotic challenge on Conor Gallagher.

Any faint hopes of a dramatic equalizer were dashed three minutes from time as Mathys Tel’s terrific solo strike ended the contest and condemned Chelsea to their third Premier League loss this season.

Morgan Rogers (center) struggled in a new role. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesPrior to Saturday’s derby, Chelsea had played just one match without Pedro spearheading their fearsome forward triumvirate in the Premier League this season. That outing ended in a 3–0 defeat to Brentford—the only game in which the Blues hadn’t scored during their first nine under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s eight goal involvements have been crucial for Chelsea, but the Brazilian’s significance stretches far beyond his output. He offers Alonso a necessary focal point at the top of his fluid 3-4-2-1 system, one which links seamlessly with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers.

Without Pedro, as was the case at the Gtech Community Stadium, Chelsea found themselves short of ideas. Instead of using Danny Welbeck as an orthodox center forward, Alonso gambled on Rogers at No. 9, supported closely by Palmer and 19-year-old Geovany Quenda. Their lack of cohesion proved a stumbling block during a tepid first half, which yielded just four shots and 0.25 expected goals.

Alonso resisted the temptation to alter his misfiring forward unit for much of the second half, even when the same issues played out time and time again. Eventually, the Chelsea boss cracked, introducing Estêvão in the 72nd minute, but their struggles persisted without a traditional No. 9.
Welbeck arrived in the closing stages, but the damage had already been done. With Chelsea trailing and down to 10 men, there was nothing the veteran could do to spare the blushes.

There are plenty of questions for Alonso to answer after a disastrous display and result against their London foes. One of those is how to organize his attack without Pedro, whose return date remains unknown.
Quenda was a surprise starter for Chelsea. / Ryan Pierse/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Mike Penders—5.8: Entirely to blame for Tottenham’s opener as he punched a routine cross into his own goal. A disastrous moment on his first Premier League start.
CB: Josh Acheampong—5.9: Given a tough ride by Mathys Tel and the overlapping Andy Robertson, with the former beating him as he raced through on goal to double Tottenham’s lead.
CB: Maxence Lacroix—6.7: Lacroix racked up an impressive number of defensive contributions, but Chelsea’s defense was pretty dire for the most part. Spurs played through them remarkably easily.
CB: Levi Colwill—6.5: Solid enough in his individual duels, but was unable to hold an underperforming rearguard together.
RWB: Pedro Neto—6.8: Often Chelsea’s brightest spark in the final third, although that’s hardly saying much.
CM: Moisés Caciedo—6.6: Thundered into challenges with typical ferocity, aided by the sodden turf. On the ball, however, Caicedo was far less impactful.
CM: Jordan Henderson—6.4: The 36-year-old was unable to match the impact he made during the 5–1 win over Bournemouth in his most recent home appearance. An unspectacular showing.
